key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that a domain-tuned RAG system can deliver correct, pedagogically useful explanations for theoretical computer science topics where proof style and notation vary widely.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical blueprint for building AI tutoring systems that combine curated technical corpora, notation-aware retrieval, and pedagogical ranking for difficult STEM subjects.
method: Built a TCS-specific knowledge base from textbooks, 847 lecture slides, 312 solved problems, 156 proof templates, and 89 worksheets.
Used mathematical entity recognition, notation-aware retrieval, and pedagogical re-ranking to improve answer quality.
Evaluated on 179 exam-style questions across asymptotic analysis, recurrences, DP, graph algorithms, NP-completeness, sorting, and divide-and-conquer.
evidence_signal: On 179 curated questions, AlgoRAG reported 100% success, 38.0 s mean response time, ROUGE-1 F1 of 0.0963, ROUGE-L F1 of 0.0683, and pedagogical quality of 0.7620.
watch_item: BLEU-4 was zero and the system appears to rely on curated domain resources, so results may not generalize well to broader or less-structured theory topics without further validation.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
